div.head: I Cn 2.4
div.ab: And þæt is þonne ærest, þæt he his agenne wer Criste ⁊ þam cyningce gesylle, ⁊ mid þam hine sylfne inlagie to bote.
And þæt is þonne ærost, þæt he his agenne wær Cryste ⁊ þam cyningce gesylle, ⁊ mid þam hyne sylfne inlagie to bote.
Et hoc tunc imprimis sit, ut weram suam (pretium natalis sui) Christo persoluat et regi, et per eam (hoc) se inlegiet ad emendandum.
And þæt is þonne ærest, þæt he his agenne wer Criste ⁊ þam cyningce gesylle ⁊ mid þam hine sylfne inlagie to bote.
And þæt is þonne ærest: þæt he his agenne wer Criste and þam cyningce gesylle, and mid þam hine sylfne inlagie to bote.
And the first condition is, that he shall give his own wergeld to Christ and to the king and by that means obtain the legal right to offer compensation.
And this is first: that he pay his own wergild to Christ and the king, and thereby make himself eligible to pay compensation.
und nämlich zuerst nun, dass er sein eigenes Wergeld der Kirche und dem König zahle und hiermit sich selbst in den Friedensgenuss einkaufe zur Bussfähigkeit.
and namely, first, that he pay his own wergild to Christ and to the king, and thereby buy himself back into the law so as to be allowed to make amends.
div.note: In G, ‘⁊ þam’ was written twice but erased. 2.4 is missing from the Instituta Cnuti. Liebermann compares VIII Atr 2.
